cards.text: Jeremiah, a prophet of the LORD, has a word about the prophets, and friend, it's hitting him HARD. He says his heart is broken within him and all his bones tremble.

cards.question: Jeremiah says he's become like a drunkard, like a man overcome by wine. What does he say has done this to him?

answers.text: The LORD and His holy words

cards.text: Then Jeremiah looks at the land. It's full of adulterers, and because of the curse the land mourns and the pastures of the wilderness have dried up.

cards.question: Jeremiah says that in the land, power is being used the way it should be.

cards.text: Now the LORD Himself speaks. And friend, NOBODY gets a pass.

cards.question: The LORD says both prophet and ___ are ungodly, and He has found their wickedness even in His ___.

cards.text: So what's coming? Their path will become slick, the LORD says. Friend, I once hopped across a counter covered in spilled sprinkles, gold base and all, and I went DOWN.

cards.question: On that slick path, what does the LORD say happens to these prophets and priests?

answers.text: They're driven into darkness and fall
They find their way back home

cards.text: He'll bring disaster on them in the year of their punishment. Then the LORD looks at the prophets of Samaria, and what He saw there was an offensive thing.

cards.question: The prophets of Samaria prophesied by ___ and led the LORD's people Israel astray.

cards.text: Now, Jerusalem's prophets? Oh, friend. Samaria's was offensive, but the LORD says what He's seen among Jerusalem's prophets is a horrible thing.

cards.question: What does the LORD say the prophets of Jerusalem do?

answers.text: Commit adultery and walk in lies
Bow to golden calves at Bethel
Refuse to speak His name aloud

cards.question: The prophets of Jerusalem strengthen the hands of evildoers. Because of that, people are turning their backs on wickedness.
To the LORD, these prophets are all like ___, and the people of Jerusalem are like Gomorrah.

cards.text: So the LORD of Hosts says He'll feed these prophets wormwood and give them poisoned water to drink.

cards.question: Why does the LORD of Hosts say this about the prophets of Jerusalem?

answers.text: Ungodliness spread from them through the land
They moved their altars out to Samaria
They stopped teaching the priests the law

cards.text: Now the LORD of Hosts has a word for the people these prophets have been prophesying to.

cards.question: The LORD of Hosts tells the people to listen closely to the words of these prophets.
The LORD says these prophets are filling the people with false hopes. Where do their visions come from?

answers.text: From the elders at the gate

cards.text: And these prophets have a favorite line. They keep using it on those who despise the LORD and on everyone who walks in the stubbornness of his own heart.

cards.question: What do these prophets keep telling everyone who walks in the stubbornness of his own heart?

answers.text: No harm will come to you
Turn back while you still can
The LORD has seen your sin

cards.text: That's a smoke alarm that just yells "Everything's FINE" louder and louder. But the LORD asks which of them has stood in His council to see and hear His word, and who has given heed to His word and obeyed it.

cards.question: Then the LORD says to look: His ___ has gone out with fury, a whirlwind swirling down on the heads of the wicked.
The LORD says His anger will turn back before He has fully accomplished the purposes of His heart.

cards.text: In the days to come, the LORD says, you will understand this clearly.

cards.question: The LORD says He never ___ these prophets, yet they have run with their message.

cards.text: He didn't speak to them, yet they prophesied. That's a guy strolling into my bakery in an apron yelling "Papa SENT me!" when Papa did NOT send him.

cards.question: These prophets never stood in the LORD's council. If they had, what does He say they would have done?

answers.text: Turned His people from their evil ways
Gone off to prophesy in Samaria

cards.text: And that's where we'll set this batch down for now. Hang on, friend, the LORD's not done talking about these prophets.

findings.problem: The card says the prophets have one 'favorite line' that they use on both groups. Verse 17 gives two different lines: to those who despise the LORD, 'The LORD says that you will have peace,' and to the stubborn, 'No harm will come to you.' No card ever tells the 'you will have peace' line, so the baker misses that detail. Cards 5 and 6 only cover the stubborn line.

rule.text: Retelling: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: Because the 'peace' line is folded into a single line, the walkthrough skips an important detail of verse 17: what the prophets tell those who despise the LORD.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: 'NOBODY gets a pass' goes beyond verse 11, which names prophet and priest. This is a storyteller's line, not a joke, so it stretches the text.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'From dreams in the night' is close to the right answer. The false prophets' dreams come from their own minds too (the next passage, Jer 23:25-27, ties their dreams to the deceit of their own hearts). A baker could argue it's right.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: Stop 1 has only one joke (card 7). The other story cards (1, 3, 5, 9, 11, 15) are mostly plain paraphrase or mild reactions. They read like a narrator rather than laugh-out-loud Papa Dorin.

rule.text: But he is FUNNY. Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The card is a bare paraphrase of verse 20 with none of Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The last story card is only the 'story isn't over' line and tells no verse, but it cites Jeremiah 23:22.
findings.question: When the last story card is only the 'story isn't over' line and tells no verse, what should its 'verses' field cite? Should it be the last verse of the passage, the verses of the card before it, or something else?
